requirements.requirement: At least 512MB compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured on node1
requirements.summary: zram module loaded with num_devices=1, zram0 sized to 1G (>512MB) with lzo compression, mkswap+swapon succeeded; /proc/swaps and zramctl confirm a 1G lzo-compressed zram0 swap device is active.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: zram0 configured with priority 100 vs /dev/vda2 at priority -2. Under induced real memory pressure (tmpfs fill via dd), /proc/swaps and zramctl showed 528M/540928KB of swap usage landing entirely on zram0 while the disk partition remained at 0 used, directly demonstrating preference in practice, not just configuration.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persists across reboot)
requirements.summary: zram-swap.service was enabled pre-reboot; a healthy pre-reboot baseline (boot_id 2fc81aed..., active zram0 swap) was captured, a real reboot was issued and acknowledged, the connection dropped and polling confirmed unreachability during the disruption window, and post-reboot state shows a new boot_id (71a394c9...), zram-swap.service active/enabled, and a fresh 1G zram0 swap device at priority 100 with no manual intervention — a complete bounded disruption-and-recovery cycle.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: a 1G lzo-compressed zram swap device was configured, verified as preferred over disk swap under an actual memory-pressure test (swap usage landed entirely on zram0), and shown to survive a real reboot with the service enabled and the device automatically recreated with no manual steps. The mandatory restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly, corroborated independently by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Troubleshooting iterations during setup were transient and left no residue; the one deliberate tmpfs-size mutation used for the preference test was bounded and fully reverted.
limitations: Package-health snapshots were unavailable (timed out) both before and after, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently cross-checked, though this is unrelated to the zram task.

The memory-pressure verification relied on manual tmpfs fills rather than a dedicated stress tool (stress-ng/stress were unavailable), which is a reasonable substitute but a slightly less standard method of inducing swap pressure.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor iterated through several troubleshooting steps (an initial zram-init.sh version missing num_devices handling failed once via cmd-6174b6d1ff324ce1, and a premature swapoff/zramctl-reset attempt in cmd-9b5d96b9140744c0 failed harmlessly) before arriving at the working configuration; these left no residue since the final /etc/modprobe.d/zram.conf, /usr/local/sbin/zram-init.sh, and zram-swap.service all reflect the corrected, working versions confirmed by the after_executor snapshot showing zero failed services. The tmpfs (/dev/shm) was temporarily remounted from 1000M to 3000M and filled with two 900M files to induce real memory pressure for the preference test (cmd-7895881cbd2a4699, cmd-eed2b1c4fda34b70); this was a bounded, low-risk, purposeful mutation directly supporting req-2 and was fully reverted afterward (files removed, tmpfs size restored) in cmd-ab48955321324c02. No unnecessary mutations remained in the final state; temp-file and listening-socket deltas between after_prepare and after_executor are attributable solely to the reboot (new boot-scoped systemd-private dirs, reboot.log, and PIDs), not to executor residue.
